page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c3d server family. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B14 processor, featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; the PassMark memory score is in the bottom 10%, with uncached read and write memory bandwidths limited to 37.53 GB/sec and 15.4 GB/sec respectively. Computational tasks like software compilation and ray tracing also register in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3d-highcpu-4 offers dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources at a lower entry cost, but presents a clear tradeoff in memory density and multi-threaded scaling. It is best suited for lightweight, compute-bound workloads that rely on single-thread execution speed rather than high memory throughput or massive parallelization. Suitable workloads include basic web serving, single-threaded data processing, and lightweight utility scripting.
